dedupe_keys.name: columbia university synthetic power grid with geographical coordinates western interconnection

description: This data set is a synthetic power grid with geographical coordinates generated from the statistical properties of the US Western Interconnection. It was produced by Saleh Soltan, Alexander Loh and Gil Zussman in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Columbia University and published on DR POWER, the Data Repository for Power system Open models With Evolving Resources, with papers describing the generation method and evaluation. Four CSV tables give bus locations as longitude and latitude, lines with end buses and a length usable as reactance, supply values in megawatts at each node, and a further table of network data, generated with stated parameters (c = 55, eta = 0.5, beta = -2.5, gamma = 1.5). Coverage is a synthetic network spread over the Western Interconnection area. The tables are downloadable from DR POWER (2018) under the GNU GPL 3.0 at no cost. Caveats: the grid is synthetic, lines use length as a proxy for reactance, and there are no generator or time-series details. Simulation uses are power flow and cascading failure studies on geographically embedded networks. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
